definition: Mechanisms, rules, or filters put in place around an AI system to constrain its behavior and prevent harmful, incorrect, or off-policy outputs.
details: Guardrails can operate at multiple levels, including input filtering, output filtering, and behavioral constraints built into the model itself through training, and are a common component of production LLM applications.
story: Picture a parachute packed by a second pair of hands: nobody plans to need it, but everyone is glad it was checked. The idea is simple: before something powerful is let loose, someone checks that it will not do real harm to real people. It is the habit of asking, before every launch, what could go wrong — and then doing something about it. Caution is not the enemy of progress — it is the reason progress gets to keep going. And that is Guardrails — the reason we can move fast without breaking things, or people.
